title: Deployment Readiness Sprint — Facilitator Script & Slide Notes
audience: Customer technical leads, product owners, vendor SRE/infra reps, Redwood SEs
content:
Purpose and context:
This doc is a facilitator-first script and slide-by-slide note set for a 2-hour customer-facing sprint focused on validating deployment readiness for a proof-of-concept (POC). The goal is to align on success criteria, validate integration touchpoints, confirm security and networking requirements, and produce a concrete cutover checklist and owner list by the end of the session.

High-level objectives (what success looks like by EOD):
- Signed alignment on acceptance criteria for the POC (SLOs, data boundaries, throughput targets).
- Clear list of integration tasks and owners (API contracts, auth, data flows).
- Deployment runbook skeleton with pre-checks, rollback triggers, and monitoring knobs.
- Risk register with mitigation actions and an action owner/timeline for each item.

Prework for customer (send 3 days before):
- Share light-weight survey: current infra (VPC CIDRs, egress rules), expected peak RPS, data residency constraints.
- Provide sample payloads and example prompts for the workload.
- Request a brief (1 slide) diagram of where Redwood endpoints will sit in their architecture.

Agenda (120 minutes total)
- 0:00–0:10 (10m) — Welcome + objectives + quick introductions (facilitator). 1-min intro per attendee, note expectations.
- 0:10–0:25 (15m) — Current state & constraints (customer). Invite customer to present pre-submitted diagram and constraints. Clarify any unknowns.
- 0:25–0:40 (15m) — POC scope and acceptance criteria (facilitator lead). Review proposed SLOs, throughput, and quality metrics. Use whiteboard to capture must-have vs nice-to-have.
- 0:40–1:05 (25m) — Integration surface mapping (breakout triads). Small breakout groups (customer infra, customer app owner, Redwood SE) to map call flows, auth, and data handling. Deliverable: sequence diagram sketch.
- 1:05–1:20 (15m) — Breakouts report back + consolidation (facilitator). Capture API endpoints, auth mechanisms, and any proxies/CDN that will be in path.
- 1:20–1:40 (20m) — Deployment runbook walkthrough (facilitator). Draft pre-checks, deployment steps, smoke tests, monitoring pages, rollback criteria. Assign preliminary owners.
- 1:40–1:55 (15m) — Risk register & mitigation commitments (group). Identify top 5 risks with probability/impact and immediate mitigations.
- 1:55–2:00 (5m) — Next steps, action owners, and meeting close. Confirm follow-up cadence and artifact owners.

Slide-by-slide outline + speaker prompts (speaker notes):
Slide 1 — Title & working agenda (Facilitator)
- Prompt: "Thanks everyone. Quick round of names and what you want to get from today — 1 sentence each."
- Visual: 3-line agenda and target outputs.

Slide 2 — POC goal & scope (Facilitator)
- Prompt: "This POC aims to validate X: latency under Yms at Z RPS and secure private routing to your VPC. Anything missing?"
- Visual: 2 columns: in-scope / out-of-scope.

Slide 3 — Customer architecture snapshot (Customer presenter)
- Prompt: "Walk us through the diagram you shared. Call out where authentication, logging, and ingress/egress live."
- Visual: Customer diagram placeholder; note areas to markup.

Slide 4 — Proposed acceptance criteria (Facilitator)
- Prompt: "Here are ALT suggested SLOs and quality checks — let's mark which are 'must' and 'nice'."
- Visual: table: metric | threshold | owner | verification method.

Slide 5 — Integration surface map (Breakout deliverable)
- Prompt: "Focus on concrete API endpoints, expected payloads, secrets management, and CORS or proxy layers."
- Visual: blank sequence diagram to fill.

Slide 6 — Auth and secrets (Facilitator)
- Prompt: "Confirm auth approach: API keys (hosted), mTLS, or token exchange. Does customer use internal KMS/HSM?"
- Visual: comparison bullets and tradeoffs.

Slide 7 — Network & egress checklist (Facilitator)
- Prompt: "Specific CIDRs, peering, firewall rules, and proxy egress expectations — we need these details for dedicated/private deploys."
- Visual: checklist with quick-yes/no columns.

Slide 8 — Deployment runbook draft (Facilitator)
- Prompt: "Walk the steps: pre-checks, staging deploy, canary, smoke tests, metrics to watch, rollback triggers."
- Visual: numbered steps with owner initials.

Slide 9 — Monitoring & observability (Customer + Redwood)
- Prompt: "Which dashboards are required? Token-level latency/cost, tail latency, error classes, and alert thresholds."
- Visual: quick mock of dashboard tiles.

Slide 10 — Risk register (Facilitator)
- Prompt: "Read out 3–5 risks we surfaced and suggested mitigations — call out exposures that need exec attention."
- Visual: risk table: risk | prob | impact | mitigation | owner.

Slide 11 — Action plan & ownership (Facilitator)
- Prompt: "Who owns what deliverable and when will it be done? Let's set realistic due dates for the runbook, network changes, and test payloads."
- Visual: action table with owners and due dates.

Slide 12 — Closing & follow-ups (Facilitator)
- Prompt: "Confirm next checkpoint (usually 3–5 business days) and artifact owners for runbook, test scripts, and monitoring links."

Facilitation tactics & tips:
- Set norms up-front: keep cameras on for the first 10 minutes, limit side-conversations; use the virtual whiteboard for diagram edits.
- Timebox strictly: call for BEAM (Backlog, Explain, Action, Move-on) when a topic stalls.
- For breakout groups: assign a scribe and a presenter. Ask triads to produce a single sticky note with top 3 takeaways.
- Use the "parking lot" for out-of-scope technical deep dives; capture owners and follow-up dates.

Decision checkpoints (explicit, call-and-respond):
- Finalize SLO thresholds (must be agreed upon by customer product/ops and Redwood SE).
- Confirm auth method and secret rotation cadence.
- Approve network changes window and rollback policy.

Deliverables to be produced within 48 hours after session:
- Deployment runbook v0.1 (Redwood SE + customer infra owner).
- Integration sequence diagram (customer app owner).
- Test payloads & sample traffic generator script (Redwood SE).
- Monitoring dashboard link and alert thresholds (joint).
- Risk register with owners and mitigation deadlines.

POC acceptance criteria checklist (example):
- Functional: end-to-end request/response verified using sanctioned test payloads.
- Performance: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms at target throughput of N RPS for sustained 5-minute window.
- Reliability: error rate < 0.5% during peak test window.
- Security: traffic routes through approved VPC path and secrets stored in customer's KMS or Redwood-managed secret store with agreed RA.
- Observability: dashboards populated with token-level latency, error classes and billing telemetry; alerts firing in staging to validate thresholds.

Risks we commonly see and suggested mitigations:
- Unavailable network egress (mitigate: pre-provision firewall rules + test before cutover).
- Auth token mis-rotation (mitigate: short-lived token + test rotation during staging).
- Large payloads causing OOM on canary (mitigate: sample payload set + memory profiling).
- Misaligned SLO expectations (mitigate: run realistic QPS test and baseline metrics).

Quick templates for actions captured during session (copy into Confluence):
- Action ID | owner | short description | due date | status
- Example: ACT-01 | Marcus Lee | Provide staging CIDR and egress rule list | 2024-09-25 | open

Post-session checklist for facilitator:
- Convert whiteboard artifacts into a single runbook draft and post to shared Confluence page within 48 hours.
- Populate action tracker and ping owners for acceptance.
- Schedule follow-up checkpoint (30–60 minutes) to validate runbook changes.

Notes to facilitator (do not read verbatim):
- If customers are unsure on SLO numbers, default to conservative thresholds we can iterate down from after cost/latency testing.
- Keep legal/security folks informed early if data classification or logging retention will be an issue.
- For Dedicated/Private options, confirm the customer's ability to accept certificate-based authentication or whether Redwood must broker.

End of document.
